# Exploring the Penguins Data

In this section you will explore the `penguins` dataset by creating multiple
types of plots. As you are creating you plots, please don't forget to (1) give
your plots reader friendly axes labels, and. (2) follow good code formatting!

## Step 0: Setup Chunk
In the empty code chunk at the top of the document, add the correct packages and label the code chunk as `setup`.  

- `tidyverse` or `ggplot2`  
- `palmerpenguins` 

## Step 1: Barchart

Use `ggplot2` to plot the frequency of each penguin `species`. 

```{r}
#| label: barchart
ggplot(data = penguins) + 
  geom_bar(aes(x = species))
```


<!-- Change roles (Computer becomes Coder)! -->

## Step 2: Histogram or Density Curve

Use `ggplot2` to plot the distribution of bill lengths for the penguins included in the dataset.

```{r}
#| label: histogram-or-density
ggplot(data= penguins) +
  geom_histogram(aes(x=bill_length_mm))
```

<!-- Change roles (Computer becomes Coder)! -->

## Step 3: Scatterplot

Use `ggplot2` to plot the relationship between the length of a penguin's bill (`bill_length_mm`) and the depth of their bill (`bill_depth_mm`).

```{r}
#| label: scatterplot
ggplot(data= penguinss, mapping=aes(x=bill_length_mm, y=bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_point()

```

## Step 4: Add a Trend Line

Add a **linear** trend line to the scatterplot you made above! 
```{r}
#| label: scatterplot + trend
ggplot(data = penguins, mapping=aes(x=bill_length_mm, y=bill_depth_mm)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = lm)

```

<!-- Change roles (Computer becomes Coder)! -->

## Step 5: Adding A Categorical Variable

Building off of the plot you made in Step 4, add an aesthetic to differentiate
the species of the penguins in the scatterplot by color.

```{r}
#| label: scatterplot-with-one-categorical-variable
ggplot(data = penguins, mapping =aes(x=bill_length_mm, y=bill_depth_mm , color = species)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = lm)
```

<!-- Change roles (Computer becomes Coder)! -->

## Step 6: Adding Another Categorical Variable

Building off of the plot you made in Step 5, add the location of the penguins
( `island`) to your visualization. There may be more than one method to address
this, however, one method will more easily allow you to address the questions
below.

```{r}
#| label: scatterplot-with-two-categorical-variables
ggplot(data = penguins, mapping =aes(x=bill_length_mm, y=bill_depth_mm , color = species)) +
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(method = lm)+
  facet_wrap (~island)
```


<!-- Change roles (Computer becomes Coder)! -->

# Canvas Quiz

Working together as a team, use the plots you both created to address the
following questions below, then use your answers to individually respond to the questions in the Canvas quiz:

1.  Which species of penguins is represented the **least** in the `penguins` data set?

>chinstrap

2.  What is the most frequent bill length seen in these data? (Approximate to the nearest 5mm)  

>45

3.  Which species of penguins are found on Biscoe Island?  

>adelie and gentoo

4.  Which species of penguins are found on Dream Island?  

>adelie and chinstrap

5.  Which species of penguins are found on Torgersen Island?  

>adelie
